metadata.title: Refined Absorption: A New Proof of the Existence Conjecture and its Applications to Extremal and Probabilistic Design Theory

nodes.name: Steiner Triple System
nodes.statement: A set of triples of an $n$-set $X$ such that every pair in $X$ is in exactly one triple; equivalently, a decomposition of the edges of $K_n$ into edge-disjoint triangles.

nodes.name: $(n,q,r)$-Steiner System
nodes.statement: A set $S$ of $q$-subsets of an $n$-set $X$ such that each $r$-subset of $X$ is contained in exactly one element of $S$; equivalently, a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $K_n^r$.

nodes.name: $(n,q,r,\lambda)$-Design
nodes.statement: A set $S$ of $q$-subsets of an $n$-set $X$ such that every $r$-subset of $X$ belongs to exactly $\lambda$ elements of $S$; equivalently, a decomposition of the multigraph $\lambda*K_q^r$ into edge-disjoint cliques.

nodes.name: $F$-decomposition and $F$-packing
nodes.statement: Given hypergraphs $F$ and $G$, an $F$-decomposition of $G$ is a partition of the edges of $G$ into copies of $F$; an $F$-packing is a set of pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $F$.

nodes.name: $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-graph
nodes.statement: An $r$-graph $G$ is $K_q^r$-divisible if for all $i\in \{0,1,\ldots, r-1\}$, $\binom{q-i}{r-i} \mid |\{e\in G: S\subseteq e\}|$ for all subsets $S$ of $V(G)$ of size $i$.

nodes.name: Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-graph. An $r$-graph $A$ is a $K_q^r$-absorber for $L$ if $V(L)$ is independent in $A$ and both $A$ and $A\cup L$ admit $K_q^r$-decompositions.

nodes.name: Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: An $r$-graph $A$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber for an $r$-graph $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{F}_A$ and decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ if $X$ and $A$ are edge-disjoint and for every $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, $\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\subseteq \mathcal{F}_A$ is a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $A\cup L$.

nodes.name: $C$-refined Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: A $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ is $C$-refined if every edge of $X\cup A$ is in at most $C$ elements of the decomposition family $\mathcal{F}_A$.

nodes.name: Booster
nodes.statement: A $K_q^r$-booster is an $r$-graph $B$ along with two $K_q^r$-decompositions $\mathcal{B}_{\rm on},\mathcal{B}_{\rm off}$ of $B$ such that $\mathcal{B}_{\rm on}\cap \mathcal{B}_{\rm off} = \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Integral $K_q^r$-Decomposition
nodes.statement: An assignment $\Phi$ of integers to copies of $K_q^r$ in $K_{V(L)}^r$ such that $\sum_{Q\ni e} \Phi(Q) = +1$ for all $e\in L$ and $\sum_{Q\ni e} \Phi(Q) = 0$ for all $e\in K_{V(L)}^r\setminus L$.

nodes.name: Anti-edge
nodes.statement: An anti-edge $e^-$, also denoted ${\rm AntiEdge}_q^r(e)$, is a clique minus the edge $e$.

nodes.name: Fake-Edge
nodes.statement: For a set $f$ of $r$ vertices, ${\rm FakeEdge}_q^r(f)$ consists of $q-r$ new vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_{q-r}$ together with anti-edges $\{{\rm AntiEdge}_q^r(T): T\in \binom{f\cup \{x_i\}}{r}\setminus\{f\}\}$.

nodes.name: Refiner
nodes.statement: An $r$-graph $R$ is a $K_q^r$-refiner of $X$ if $V(X)=V(R)$, $X$ and $R$ are edge-disjoint, and for every $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$ there exists a decomposition of $R\cup L$ into $K_q^r$-divisible subgraphs.

nodes.name: Supergraph System
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{W}=(W_H: H\in \mathcal{H})$ where each $W_H$ is a supergraph of $H$ with $(V(W_H)\setminus V(H))\cap V(J)=\emptyset$ and $V(W_H)\cap V(W_{H'})\setminus V(J)=\emptyset$ for $H\ne H'$. $C$-bounded means $\max\{e(W_H), v(W_H)\}\le C$.

nodes.name: Embedding of a Supergraph System
nodes.statement: Given $G\supseteq J$, an embedding of $\mathcal{W}$ into $G$ is a map $\phi: V(\bigcup \mathcal{W})\hookrightarrow V(G)$ preserving edges with $\phi(v)=v$ for all $v\in V(J)$.

nodes.name: Decomposition Threshold $\delta_{K_q^r}$
nodes.statement: $\delta_{K_q^r} := \limsup_{n\to \infty} \delta_{K_q^r}(n)/n$, where $\delta_{K_q^r}(n)$ is the smallest $d$ such that every $K_q^r$-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge d$ has a $K_q^r$-decomposition.

nodes.name: Fractional $K_q^r$-Decomposition and Threshold
nodes.statement: An assignment of non-negative weights to copies of $K_q^r$ in $G$ summing to $1$ along each edge. The fractional threshold $\delta^*_{K_q^r}$ is the infimum of $c$ such that every $r$-graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge c\cdot v(G)$ admits a fractional $K_q^r$-decomposition.

nodes.name: $(j,i)$-configuration and Girth
nodes.statement: A $(j,i)$-configuration in $\mathcal{P}$ is a set of $i$ elements of $\mathcal{P}$ spanning at most $j$ ground vertices. Girth of an $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system is the smallest $g\ge 2$ such that it contains a $((q-r)g+r, g)$-configuration.

nodes.name: Collective Girth of an Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: A $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ has collective girth at least $g$ if for every $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, $\mathcal{Q}_A(L)$ has girth at least $g$.

nodes.name: Rooted Girth of a Booster
nodes.statement: For a $K_q^r$-packing $\mathcal{B}$ and $S\subseteq V(G)$, the rooted girth at $S$ is the smallest $g$ such that $\exists \mathcal{B}'\subseteq \mathcal{B}$ with $|\mathcal{B}'|=g$ and $|V(\bigcup \mathcal{B}')\setminus S|<(q-r)g$. For a booster $B$ with $S\in \mathcal{B}_{\rm off}$, the rooted girth is the minimum of the girths of $\mathcal{B}_{\rm on}$, $\mathcal{B}_{\rm off}$, and the rooted girth of $\mathcal{B}_{\rm on}$ at $V(S)$.

nodes.name: Random $q$-uniform Hypergraph $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ and Threshold
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ is the random $n$-vertex $q$-uniform hypergraph in which each $q$-set is included independently with probability $p$. A function $p^*(n)$ is a threshold for an increasing property $\mathcal{P}$ if $\mathrm{Prob}[\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n_i,p)\in \mathcal{P}]\to 0$ for $p=o(p^*)$ and $\to 1$ for $p=\omega(p^*)$.

nodes.name: $\sigma$-spread Distribution
nodes.statement: A probability distribution on $K_q$-decompositions $\mathcal{H}$ of $G$ is $\sigma$-spread if $\mathrm{Prob}[\mathcal{S}\subseteq \mathcal{H}]\le \sigma^{|\mathcal{S}|}$ for all $K_q$-packings $\mathcal{S}$ of $G$.

nodes.name: $C$-low-weight Fractional Decomposition
nodes.statement: A fractional $F$-decomposition of $G$ on $n$ vertices is $C$-low-weight if every copy of $F$ in $G$ has weight at most $\frac{C}{n^{v(F)-2}}$.

nodes.name: Existence Conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $q>r\ge 2$ and $\lambda\ge 1$. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $\binom{q-i}{r-i}\mid \lambda\binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0\le i\le r-1$, then there exists a design with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Existence Conjecture (Keevash)
nodes.statement: The Existence Conjecture is true.

nodes.name: Nibble for Designs
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \beta\in (0,1), \exists \alpha\in (0,1)$ s.t. for $D$ large enough: if $G\subseteq K_n^r$ and $\mathcal{H}\subseteq K_q^r(G)$ with every edge in $D(1\pm D^{-\beta})$ cliques and every pair in at most $D^{1-\beta}$ cliques, then there is a $K_q^r$-packing of $G$ of size $\ge \frac{e(G)}{\binom{q}{r}}(1-D^{-\alpha})$.
assumptions: every edge of $G$ is in $D(1\pm D^{-\beta})$ cliques of $\mathcal{H}$
every pair of edges of $G$ is in at most $D^{1-\beta}$ cliques of $\mathcal{H}$
conclusions: There exists a $K_q^r$-packing of $G$ of size $\ge \frac{e(G)}{\binom{q}{r}}(1-D^{-\alpha})$

nodes.name: Nibble for Designs (specific $D$)
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \rho\in (0,1], \exists \alpha\in (0,1)$ s.t. for $n$ large: if every edge of $G\subseteq K_n^r$ is in $(\rho \pm n^{-1/3})\binom{n}{q-r}$ cliques of $\mathcal{H}\subseteq K_q^r(G)$, then $\exists$ a $K_q^r$-packing of $G$ of size $\ge \frac{e(G)}{\binom{q}{r}}(1-n^{-\alpha})$.
assumptions: every edge of $G$ in $(\rho\pm n^{-1/3})\binom{n}{q-r}$ cliques of $\mathcal{H}$
conclusions: There is a $K_q^r$-packing of $G$ of size $\ge \frac{e(G)}{\binom{q}{r}}(1-n^{-\alpha})$

nodes.name: Existence of Absorbers
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1$: if $L$ is a $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-graph, then there exists a $K_q^r$-absorber for $L$.

nodes.name: Efficient Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \exists C\ge 1$: if $X\subseteq K_n^r$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(X)\le \frac{n}{C}$, then there is a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(A)\le C\cdot \max\{\Delta_{r-1}(X), n^{1-1/r}\log n\}$.

nodes.name: Refined Efficient Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \exists C\ge 1$: if $X\subseteq K_n^r$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(X)\le n/C$, then there is a $C$-refined $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(A)\le C\max\{\Delta_{r-1}(X), n^{1-1/r}\log n\}$.

nodes.name: Reserves Lemma
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \exists \gamma\in (0,1)$ s.t. for $n$ large: if $p\in [n^{-\gamma},1)$, then there exists $X\subseteq K_n^r$ with $\Delta(X)\le 2pn$ s.t. every $e\in K_n^r\setminus X$ is in $\ge \frac{1}{2}p^{\binom{q}{r}-1}\binom{n}{q-r}$ $K_q^r$-cliques of $X\cup \{e\}$.
conclusions: every $e\in K_n^r\setminus X$ is in $\ge \frac{1}{2}p^{\binom{q}{r}-1}\binom{n}{q-r}$ $K_q^r$-cliques of $X\cup \{e\}$

nodes.name: Boost Lemma
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \exists \varepsilon\in (0,1)$ s.t. for $n$ large: if $J\subseteq K_n^r$ with $\delta(J)\ge (1-\varepsilon)n$, then there is $\mathcal{H}\subseteq K_q^r(J)$ s.t. every $e\in J$ is in $(\frac{1}{2}\pm n^{-1/3})\binom{n-r}{q-r}$ cliques of $\mathcal{H}$.
conclusions: $\exists \mathcal{H}\subseteq K_q^r(J)$ such that every $e\in J$ is in $(\frac{1}{2}\pm n^{-1/3})\binom{n-r}{q-r}$ cliques of $\mathcal{H}$

nodes.name: Nibble with Reserves for Designs
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \beta\in (0,1), \exists \alpha\in (0,1)$ for $D$ large: with $G,\mathcal{H}$ as in Nibble for Designs, if $\exists X\subseteq K_n^r\setminus G$ and $\mathcal{H}'\subseteq K_q^r(G\cup X)$ with $|H\cap E(G)|=1$ for all $H\in \mathcal{H}'$, every $e\in G$ in $\ge D^{1-\alpha}$ elements of $\mathcal{H}'$ and every $e\in X$ in $\le D/\beta$ elements of $\mathcal{H}'$, then there is a $K_q^r$-packing of $G\cup X$ covering all edges of $G$.
assumptions: every $e\in G$ in $\ge D^{1-\alpha}$ elements of $\mathcal{H}'$
every $e\in X$ in $\le D/\beta$ elements of $\mathcal{H}'$
conclusions: There exists a $K_q^r$-packing of $G\cup X$ covering all edges of $G$

nodes.name: Nibble with Reserves (specific)
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r\ge 1, \rho\in (0,1], \exists \alpha\in (0,1)$ s.t. for $n$ large: with $G,\mathcal{H}$ as in Cor.~\ref{cor:NibbleDesignsSpecific}, if $\exists X\subseteq K_n^r\setminus G$ s.t. every $e\in G$ is in $\ge n^{q-r-\alpha}$ $K_q^r$-cliques of $X\cup \{e\}$, then there is a $K_q^r$-packing of $G\cup X$ covering $G$.
assumptions: $\exists X\subseteq K_n^r\setminus G$ s.t. every $e\in G$ is in $\ge n^{q-r-\alpha}$ $K_q^r$-cliques of $X\cup \{e\}$
conclusions: There is a $K_q^r$-packing of $G\cup X$ that covers all edges of $G$

nodes.name: Graver-Jurkat / Wilson Integral Decomposition
nodes.statement: Let $q>r\ge 1$. If $L$ is a $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-graph with $v(L)\ge q+r$, then there exists an integral $K_q^r$-decomposition of $L$.

nodes.name: General Embedding Lemma
nodes.statement: $\forall C>r\ge 1, \gamma\in (0,1], \exists C'\ge 1$: if $G\subseteq K_n^r$ and $J$ a multi-$r$-graph with ${\rm Simple}(J)\subseteq G$, $\Delta(J)\le n/C'$, $\mathcal{H}$ a $C$-refined family in $J$, $\mathcal{W}$ a $C$-bounded edge-intersecting supergraph system with $\ge \gamma n^{|V(W_H)\setminus V(H)|}$ embeddings of $W_H$ into $G\setminus (E(J)\setminus E(H))$ for each $H$, then there is an embedding $\phi$ of $\mathcal{W}$ into $G$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(\phi(\mathcal{W}))\le C'\Delta_{r-1}(J)$.
assumptions: $\ge \gamma n^{|V(W_H)\setminus V(H)|}$ embeddings of $W_H$ into $G\setminus (E(J)\setminus E(H))$ for each $H\in \mathcal{H}$
conclusions: There is an embedding $\phi$ of $\mathcal{W}$ into $G$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(\phi(\mathcal{W}))\le C'\cdot \Delta_{r-1}(J)$

nodes.name: Embedding Lemma (Min Degree)
nodes.statement: $\forall C>r\ge 1, \exists C'\ge 1, \varepsilon\in (0,1)$: if $G\subseteq K_n^r$ with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)n$ and $J$ a multi-$r$-graph with ${\rm Simple}(J)\subseteq G$, $\Delta(J)\le n/C'$, $\mathcal{H}$ $C$-refined and $\mathcal{W}$ $C$-bounded edge-intersecting, then there is an embedding $\phi$ of $\mathcal{W}$ into $G$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(\phi(\mathcal{W}))\le C'\Delta_{r-1}(J)$.
conclusions: There is an embedding $\phi$ of $\mathcal{W}$ into $G$ with $\Delta_{r-1}(\phi(\mathcal{W}))\le C'\cdot \Delta_{r-1}(J)$

nodes.name: Proof of Embedding Lemma (Min Degree)
nodes.statement: Choose $\varepsilon$ small enough so that $|\Phi(H)|\ge \gamma\cdot n^{|V(W_H)\setminus V(H)|}$ for all $H\in \mathcal{H}$ for some $\gamma\in (0,1)$, then apply the General Embedding Lemma~\ref{lem:EmbedGeneral}.

nodes.name: Nash-Williams' Conjecture
nodes.statement: For sufficiently large $n$: if $G$ is a $K_3$-divisible graph on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge \frac{3}{4}n$, then $G$ admits a $K_3$-decomposition.

nodes.name: Barber-Kühn-Lo-Osthus on Nash-Williams
nodes.statement: For each $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large $K_3$-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (\max\{\delta^*_{K_3}, \frac{3}{4}\}+\varepsilon)n$ admits a $K_3$-decomposition.

nodes.name: Delcourt-Postle 2021 fractional Nash-Williams
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a $K_3$-divisible graph on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge \frac{7+\sqrt{21}}{14}n$, then $G$ admits a fractional $K_3$-decomposition.

nodes.name: Folklore $K_q$-decomposition Conjecture
nodes.statement: For each integer $q\ge 4$, for sufficiently large $n$: if $G$ is a $K_q$-divisible graph on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\frac{1}{q+1})n$, then $G$ admits a $K_q$-decomposition.

nodes.name: Disproof of Folklore Conjecture
nodes.statement: $\forall q\ge 4, \exists c>1$ and infinitely many $K_q$-divisible graphs $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\frac{1}{c(q+1)})v(G)$ and no fractional $K_q$-decomposition.
conclusions: $\exists c>1$ and infinitely many $K_q$-divisible graphs $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\frac{1}{c(q+1)})v(G)$ and no fractional $K_q$-decomposition

nodes.name: Asymptotic Counterexample
nodes.statement: Let $c=\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and fix $\varepsilon>0$. For every large enough $q$, there are infinitely many $K_q$-divisible graphs $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\frac{1}{(c-\varepsilon)(q+1)})v(G)$ and no fractional $K_q$-decomposition.
conclusions: $\exists$ infinitely many $K_q$-divisible graphs $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\frac{1}{(c-\varepsilon)(q+1)})v(G)$ and no fractional $K_q$-decomposition

nodes.name: Reserves for Nash-Williams
nodes.statement: $\forall q\ge 3, \varepsilon\in (0,1), \exists \gamma\in (0,1)$ s.t. for $n$ large: let $G\subseteq K_n$ with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\frac{1}{q+1}+\varepsilon)n$. If $p\in [n^{-\gamma},1)$, then there is $X\subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X)\le 2pn$ s.t. every $e\in K_n\setminus X$ is in $\ge \frac{1}{(q+1)^q}p^{\binom{q}{2}-1}\binom{n}{q-2}$ $K_q$-cliques of $X\cup \{e\}$.
conclusions: every $e\in K_n\setminus X$ is in $\ge \frac{1}{(q+1)^q}p^{\binom{q}{2}-1}\binom{n}{q-2}$ $K_q$-cliques of $X\cup \{e\}$

nodes.name: Nash-Williams Refined Efficient Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: $\forall q\ge 3, \varepsilon\in (0,1), \exists C\ge 1$: if $X\subseteq G\subseteq K_n$ with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\frac{1}{2q-2}+\varepsilon)n$ and $\Delta(X)\le n/C$, then there is a $C$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ in $G$ with $\Delta(A)\le C\max\{\Delta(X), \sqrt{n}\log n\}$.

nodes.name: Inheritance Lemma for Minimum Degree
nodes.statement: $\forall \varepsilon\in (0,1), m\ge 1, \exists s_0$ s.t. for $s\ge s_0$ and $n$ large: let $\delta\ge 0$ and $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (\delta+\varepsilon)(n-1)$. Then for every $m$-set $M\subseteq V(G)$, there are $\ge (1-e^{-\sqrt{s}})\binom{n-m}{s-m}$ $s$-sets $S$ with $M\subseteq S$ and $\delta(G[S])\ge (\delta+\varepsilon/2)(s-1)$.

nodes.name: Nash-Williams Boosting Lemma (Constant Irregularity)
nodes.statement: $\forall q\ge 3, \varepsilon\in (0,1), \exists c\in (0,1)$ s.t. for all $\gamma\in (0,1)$ and $n$ large: if $J\subseteq K_n$ with $\delta(J)\ge (\max\{\delta^*_{K_q}, 1-\frac{1}{q+1}\}+\varepsilon)n$, then there is a family $\mathcal{H}$ of copies of $K_q$ in $J$ s.t. every $e\in J$ is in $(c\pm \gamma)\binom{n-2}{q-2}$ copies in $\mathcal{H}$.
conclusions: $\exists$ a family $\mathcal{H}$ of copies of $K_q$ in $J$ such that every $e\in J$ is in $(c\pm \gamma)\binom{n-2}{q-2}$ copies of $K_q$ in $\mathcal{H}$

nodes.name: Low-Weight Fractional Decomposition
nodes.statement: For every graph $F$ and $\varepsilon\in (0,1), \exists C\ge 1$ s.t. for $n$ large: if $G$ is an $n$-vertex graph with $\delta(G)\ge (\delta^*_F+\varepsilon)n$, then there is a $C$-low-weight fractional $F$-decomposition of $G$.

nodes.name: Erdős' High Girth Steiner Triple Systems Conjecture
nodes.statement: For every integer $g\ge 3$, every sufficiently large $K_3$-divisible complete graph admits a $K_3$-decomposition with girth at least $g$.

nodes.name: Resolution of Erdős' High Girth Conjecture
nodes.statement: Erdős' Conjecture on high girth Steiner triple systems is true.

nodes.name: High Girth Existence Conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $q>r\ge 2$. For every integer $g\ge 3$, every sufficiently large $K_q^r$-divisible complete $r$-uniform hypergraph admits a $K_q^r$-decomposition with girth $\ge g$.

nodes.name: Resolution of High Girth Existence Conjecture
nodes.statement: The High Girth Existence Conjecture is true.

nodes.name: High Rooted Girth Booster Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $q>r\ge 2$ and $g\ge 1$. If the ``High Cogirth Existence Theorem'' holds for $r':=r-1$, then there exists a $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with rooted girth $\ge g$.
conclusions: There exists a $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with rooted girth $\ge g$

nodes.name: Erdős meets Nash-Williams
nodes.statement: For every integer $g$ and any sufficiently large $n$, every $K_3$-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge \frac{3n}{4}$ admits a $K_3$-decomposition with girth at least $g$.

nodes.name: Erdős meets Nash-Williams Progress
nodes.statement: $\forall g\ge 3, \varepsilon>0$: every sufficiently large $K_3$-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (\max\{\delta^*_{K_3}, \frac{3}{4}\}+\varepsilon)n$ admits a $K_3$-decomposition with girth $\ge g$.

nodes.name: $K_q$-Generalisation of Erdős meets Nash-Williams
nodes.statement: $\forall g, q\ge 3, \varepsilon>0$: every sufficiently large $K_q$-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (\max\{\delta^*_{K_q}, 1-\frac{1}{2q-2}\}+\varepsilon)n$ admits a $K_q$-decomposition with girth $\ge g$.

nodes.name: Conjecture on $K_q$ High Girth without $\delta^*$ slack
nodes.statement: For all $g, q\ge 3, \varepsilon>0$: every sufficiently large $K_q$-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (\delta^*_{K_q}+\varepsilon)n$ admits a $K_q$-decomposition with girth $\ge g$.

nodes.name: Kang-Kelly-Kühn-Methuku-Osthus Threshold Conjecture
nodes.statement: $\forall q>r$: if $\binom{q-i}{r-i}\mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $i\in \{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ and $p=\omega(n^{-q+r}\log n)$, then a.a.s. $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ contains an $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system.

nodes.name: Existence of Steiner Systems in Sparse Random Hypergraphs
nodes.statement: $\forall q>2$: if $q-1\mid n-1$ and $\binom{q}{2}\mid \binom{n}{2}$ and $p\ge n^{-(q-6)/2}$, then a.a.s. $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ contains an $(n,q,2)$-Steiner system.

nodes.name: Spread Distribution on Steiner Decompositions
nodes.statement: $\forall q>2, \exists \beta>0$ s.t. for $n$ large: if $K_n$ is $K_q$-divisible, then there exists an $(n^{-(q-6)/2-\beta})$-spread probability distribution on $K_q$-decompositions of $K_n$.

nodes.name: Edge-Intersecting Absorbers
nodes.statement: An absorber is edge-intersecting if for every $e\in A$ there is $f\in L$ with $e\cap V(L)\subseteq f$. Edge-intersecting absorbers exist (proved by pushing $L$ one uniformity at a time onto a new vertex set first), simplifying the refine-down tracking by removing the need for refinement degree.

nodes.name: Refined Absorption Proof of the Existence Conjecture
nodes.statement: Four-step framework that combines reserves, an efficient refined omni-absorber, regularity boosting, and nibble with reserves to prove the Existence Conjecture.
input: Integer $n$ satisfying divisibility conditions, sufficiently large

nodes.name: Reserve random subset $X$
nodes.statement: Choose a random subset $X\subseteq E(K_n^r)$ uniformly with some small (well-chosen) probability $p$ so that $X$ has small max degree and many cliques.

nodes.name: Construct omni-absorber $A$
nodes.statement: Construct an omni-absorber $A$ of $X$ of small max $(r-1)$-degree via Theorem~\ref{thm:RefinedEfficientOmniAbsorber}.

nodes.name: Regularity boost $J:=K_n^r\setminus (A\cup X)$
nodes.statement: Find a set of cliques of $J=K_n^r\setminus (A\cup X)$ such that every edge of $J$ is in roughly the same dense number of cliques.

nodes.name: Apply Nibble with Reserves
nodes.statement: Apply Nibble with Reserves to find a $K_q^r$-packing of $K_n^r\setminus A$ covering $K_n^r\setminus (A\cup X)$, then extend to a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $K_n^r$ by definition of omni-absorber.

nodes.name: Short Construction of $K_q^r$-Absorbers
nodes.statement: Builds a $K_q^r$-absorber via a multi-absorber from an integral decomposition (Graver-Jurkat/Wilson), then converts it to a true absorber by inserting anti-edges and attaching anti-clique absorbers (recursive booster construction).

nodes.name: Build multi-absorber via integral decomposition
nodes.statement: Use the Graver-Jurkat/Wilson integral $K_q^r$-decomposition $\Phi$ of $L$. Positive cliques form a $K_q^r$-decomposition $\mathcal{Q}_1$ of $L\cup A$ and negative cliques form a $K_q^r$-decomposition $\mathcal{Q}_2$ of the multi-absorber $A$.

nodes.name: Transpose to negative setting via anti-edges
nodes.statement: Add an anti-edge $e^-$ for each $e\in L\cup A$ and let $A^*=\bigcup_{e\in L\cup A} e^-$. Then $\mathcal{Q}_1$ corresponds to an anti-clique decomposition of $A^*$ and $\mathcal{Q}_2$ to an anti-clique decomposition of $\bigcup_{e\in A} e^-$.

nodes.name: Build absorber for an anti-clique using boosters
nodes.statement: Construct a booster $B$ via Cauchy matrices, layer copies to form an orthogonal booster $B_o$, and attach copies $B_e$ of $B_o$ to each $Q_e$ with $e\in S$ so that the cliques $Q_e'$ form a vertex-disjoint anti-clique yielding the desired absorber decompositions.

nodes.name: Refine Down (proof of Refined Efficient Omni-Absorber)
nodes.statement: Inductive procedure that constructs a $C$-refined efficient $K_q^r$-omni-absorber by repeatedly applying the Refine Down Lemma and the Multiplicity Reduction Lemma until the remainder is on a constant-sized vertex set, where the theorem trivially holds.

nodes.name: Base $1$-uniform construction
nodes.statement: For $r=1$: let $A$ be $q\cdot |X|$ new vertices, $H_1$ a tight $q$-path on $A$, $H_2$ a tight $q$-path on $A\cup X$ with $X$ vertices interspersed every $q$ vertices; set $\mathcal{F}_A:=H_1\cup H_2$.

nodes.name: Reduce to multi-omni-absorber and refiner
nodes.statement: Reduce to multigraph version using fake-edges to remove parallel edges. Replace decomposing into cliques with decomposing into small $K_q^r$-divisible graphs via refiners.

nodes.name: Refine Down Lemma loop
nodes.statement: Apply the Refine Down Lemma to construct an efficient refined multi-refiner whose remainder lies in a smaller vertex set; alternate with Multiplicity Reduction Lemma to keep multiplicity constant; iterate until the remainder set is constant size.

nodes.name: Embed fake-edges and private absorbers
nodes.statement: Use the General Embedding Lemma to embed fake-edges (replacing multi-edges) and private absorbers (one for each fake-ish clique in the decomposition family) edge-disjointly with low max degree.

nodes.name: High Girth Omni-Absorber Construction
nodes.statement: Modification of Refine Down by embedding private rooted high-girth boosters into each clique of the decomposition family; uses Lovász Local Lemma to ensure collective girth $\ge g$ and random sparsification so configurations are not over-shrunk.

nodes.name: Spread Omni-Absorber Construction
nodes.statement: Modification of Refine Down for the spread setting that embeds spread boosters (with good randomness properties) into the decomposition family of the refined omni-absorber, then uses the Lovász Local Lemma distribution to control disjointness.
output: A $\sigma$-spread embedding of an omni-absorber into $K_n^r$

nodes.name: Minimum Degree Thresholds for $K_q^r$-decompositions
nodes.statement: What is the minimum $(r-1)$-degree that forces a $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-graph on $n$ vertices to admit a $K_q^r$-decomposition?

nodes.name: Existence of High Girth Steiner Systems
nodes.statement: Do there exist $(n,q,r)$-Steiner systems of large girth for all $q>r$ and $n$ large enough?

nodes.name: Probabilistic Thresholds for Steiner Systems
nodes.statement: What is the minimum probability $p$ such that the binomial random $q$-graph $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ contains an $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system asymptotically almost surely?

nodes.name: Determine min-degree thresholds for $K_q$- and $K_q^r$-decompositions
nodes.statement: Determine the minimum degree thresholds for $K_q$-decompositions and $K_q^r$-decompositions more generally.

nodes.name: Determine probability thresholds for $K_q$- and $K_q^r$-decompositions
nodes.statement: Determine the probability thresholds for $K_q$-decompositions and $K_q^r$-decompositions more generally.

nodes.name: Refined Absorption to Partite/Partitioned Hypergraphs
nodes.statement: Extend refined absorption to partite and partitioned hypergraphs (and more generally to all of Keevash's Designs II settings).

nodes.name: Unification of Design Theory Problems
nodes.statement: Unify the various problems (minimum degree, high girth, spread, partite, etc.) into one super theorem (possibly with tradeoffs).

nodes.name: Postle's Postulate of a Unified Theorem of Designs
nodes.statement: There exists one unified theorem of designs.
